summary: JIT ephemeral SSH key request stuck in 'Pending Manager Approval' after Okta SCIM 'manager' attribute returned as email string
description:
Issue summary: Several engineers' just-in-time (JIT) ephemeral SSH key requests remain in 'Pending Manager Approval' even after their managers click approve in the approval UI. The approval records are not being picked up by the runbook/provisioner service.

Impact: Affected engineers cannot access internal bastion for runbook work and incident response. ~8 active requests discovered, broader population unknown. Business impact: interrupts oncall response for non-critical incidents and delays routine maintenance.

Observed behavior: The approval UI shows manager action completed (timestamped). Approval queue shows approval event for the request id, but runbook-provisioner does not transition the request to 'Approved' and does not issue an ephemeral key. Audit logs show the SCIM sync transforming the Okta 'manager' attribute into an email string (e.g., "alice@example.com") rather than Okta user id or canonical SCIM reference, causing the runbook-provisioner lookup to fail (it expects manager to be an Okta 'id' or SCIM reference).

Expected behavior: Approval events should link to manager principal by Okta id / SCIM id and drive the provisioning to 'Approved' and issue SSH key.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Submit a JIT SSH access request for a user whose Okta profile has manager set.
2) Have manager approve via approval UI.
3) Observe approval entry in audit log.
4) Check runbook-provisioner logs; provisioning does not proceed and request remains Pending.
5) Inspect SCIM payload forwarded to provisioner and note manager attribute contents.
investigation_notes:
- Identity team reproduced locally: SCIM adapter commit 4f9a2d introduced a transformation that flattens manager to manager.email when manager.profile is present. This was intended to simplify a previous NA-characters bug but regressed consumers that expect SCIM reference format.
- Runbook-provisioner performs a lookup by Okta user id / SCIM ref only; codepath does not accept email string as a stable foreign key.
- No existing fallback mapping: when manager is email we attempt an email->Okta lookup via Identity API which has higher latency and rate limits; in most failing cases the lookup returned 404 due to query normalization differences (dot vs plus addressing).
- Affected requests appear clustered for employees whose Okta manager attribute was modified in the last 7 days (bulk org import on 2026-03-08).
- Cross-reference: related incident INT-314271 (identity namespace collision) was unrelated but shows prior bulk import risk patterns.
workaround:
1) Manual approval by Platform Oncall: Support engineers can manually set request state to 'Approved' in the provisioning DB (runbook-provisioner admin UI) for emergency access until fix deployed.
2) Identity team rolled back the SCIM adapter transform on staging and pushed a canary to a small subset of customers to verify behavior.
Note: manual DB state change is logged and requires follow-up audit entry.
resolution:
Partial: Rolled back identity-sync change that flattened manager to email in staging; applied hotfix (revert commit 4f9a2d) to identity-sync in prod on 2026-03-12 02:10Z. After rollback, runbook-provisioner consumed SCIM reference objects and resumed provisioning for new approvals. For stuck requests where approval event used email form, runbook-provisioner now accepts a one-time fallback email lookup (added small patch) and advanced 6 of 8 pending requests to Approved. Remaining 2 required manual DB approvals due to plus-addressing mismatch.
Follow-up: identity team will add a contract test to prevent manager attribute shape regressions and add a migration script to normalize manager fields for pending requests.
next_steps:
- Identity: add SCIM contract test (PR planned) and schedule a data normalization job for manager attributes (owner: Marco Rivera, ETA 2026-03-18).
- Provisioner: add robust email fallback path with rate-limit backoff and deterministic normalization (owner: Priya Shah, ETA 2026-03-17).
- Support: run audit on all JIT requests created between 2026-03-08 and 2026-03-12 to identify any remaining stuck items (owner: Aisha Patel, ETA 2026-03-14).
